articles.title: IBM i (OS/400) The Database Operating System
articles.summary: IBM's child, the AS/400, is an architecture that went its own way and proved systems engineering design can look completely different from other operating systems like Unix, Linux, and Windows. This system was doing abstraction and virtualization decades ago, and it's one of the most uncompromising projects in IT history. The AS/400 platform adopted the technological power of System/38 and clothed it in user-friendliness of System/36, resulting in a key assumption that protected client investment in software through the TIMI abstraction layer. This approach defined the system's identity for decades to come, allowing programs written in 1990 to run natively on servers produced this year.

articles.title: Dithered QR codes
articles.summary: Dithered QR codes involve modifying data modules in a QR code to make them look distinctive and robust against scanning errors. This is achieved by shrinking the data modules, which allows for a fair amount of flexibility before the code becomes unscannable. The process involves dividing each pixel into a three-by-three grid and storing the middle one as the data module, while the others are used for a photo. Dithering techniques such as Floyd-Steinberg dithering can be applied to improve the image quality, but error diffusion is also an important aspect of making QR codes more robust against scanning errors.
